evals.name: showcase-with-figure
evals.prompt: I shipped bulk export in our admin panel: you select rows in the users table, hit Export, and get a CSV in a toast with a download link. Exports used to be a support ticket and took a day; now 300 per week, median 4 seconds. Make me a demo page to show the team, with an animation of the flow.
evals.expected_output: A single built HTML page in the Journal look with a stageshow figure of selecting rows and exporting, a metrics table, and the page order from the example.
assertions: The page head keeps the fonts link and <style data-journal></style>, and the built file inlines journal.css
A figures/<name>.tsx exists, default-exports a component, and spreads JOURNAL on its Stage
The figure sits in figure.fig.breakout with a figcaption that says what to notice
The numbers are in table.metrics or .stats, not invented beyond what the user gave
No new colors or font families are introduced outside the journal tokens
No sentence from the search-rollout example remains
The headline states the claim as a finding (with its number when there is one), and the first screen also carries the ask or says there is none
Section headings state findings, not topics
Every number on the page traces to the prompt, the repo, or a question asked to the user; none are invented
A fresh subagent ran the comprehension check on dist/page.txt and the first-screen image, not by browsing the page
The handover message lists facts that came from inference for the user to confirm
The page states a cost or limit of the feature, not only wins
The agent never opened a built dist/*.html file

evals.name: architecture-proposal
evals.prompt: Write up a proposal page: we want to move our job queue from Postgres SKIP LOCKED polling to Redis Streams. Workers poll every 500ms today and hold connections; at peak we hit the connection limit. Options: Redis Streams (new infra), or pgbouncer plus LISTEN/NOTIFY (no new infra, but NOTIFY payload limits). I lean Redis. Need a decision from the team by next Friday.
evals.expected_output: A Journal page with an inline SVG architecture diagram in a .panel, both options in .options with Redis marked data-recommended, and the deadline in the masthead facts. No stageshow figure is needed.
assertions: The architecture is an inline SVG in .panel using dg-* classes, with the focal node marked .focus
Both options appear as .option, and the Redis option carries data-recommended
The decision deadline appears in .facts
No stageshow figure is built for a page with no product moment
The build produced dist/page.html and dist/page.preview.html
The headline states the claim as a finding (with its number when there is one), and the first screen also carries the ask or says there is none
Section headings state findings, not topics
Every number on the page traces to the prompt, the repo, or a question asked to the user; none are invented
A fresh subagent ran the comprehension check on dist/page.txt and the first-screen image, not by browsing the page
The handover message lists facts that came from inference for the user to confirm
Each option gets its strongest honest case, including the one not recommended
The agent never opened a built dist/*.html file

evals.name: metrics-report
evals.prompt: Make a page with our Q3 reliability numbers for the eng all-hands: uptime 99.95% (was 99.81%), 4 SEV1s (was 11), MTTR 38 min (was 2h10), on-call pages per week 23 (was 61). One regression: deploy frequency dropped from 41 to 33 per week because of the new review gate.
evals.expected_output: A Journal page where the numbers are the point: .stats for the headline figures, a metrics table with .good on wins and .bad on the deploy-frequency regression, and a .note explaining the regression.
assertions: Headline numbers use .stats or table.metrics, with tabular figures
The deploy-frequency regression is marked .bad and is explained in prose or a .note, not hidden
Status colors appear only on status; the clay accent is not used to mark wins
The page is checked at 1280 and 390 wide before handover
The headline states the claim as a finding (with its number when there is one), and the first screen also carries the ask or says there is none
